session_vs_memory.session_summary: Completed end-to-end open-weight VLM benchmark (Salesforce/blip-vqa-base) and nested cross-validation with question-paired uncertainty analysis. Standalone BLIP VLM scored 0.50376 MAP@3 (-0.03838 vs S550). Flat-blend (+0.00004 at w=0.05) was refuted under nested 5-fold CV (4-fold inner GroupKFold selection): true generalization delta is -0.00245 Composite MAP@3 (0.53969 vs 0.54214). In 3/5 outer folds inner CV rejected VLM (w=0.0 pure S550); in the remaining 2 folds, non-zero blends degraded on outer held-out test. Question-paired analysis (N=462) showed 12 degraded vs 5 improved (2.4x degradation ratio), cluster bootstrap 95% CI [-0.002914, +0.002140], and statistically significant degradation on seen curriculum questions (t=-2.07, p=0.0389). Open-weight VLM branch permanently closed alongside LUPI distillation, stroke density rerankers, and handwriting OCR. Champion S550 (Kaggle Ref 58084010, Public LB 0.55049, Composite CV 0.54214, SHA256 b2637c3b7a92010d3d04f41f2f4c2e91e0cc312a63d2532ab63f1d16bf90bc70) remains the locked, verified final competition entry.

evaluated_smooth_quad_3500_champion.post_mortem: Scored 0.54566 (only -0.00050 from 0.54616 peak). Forensic analysis confirmed exactly 6 borderline Rank-1 swaps involving NONE accounted for the entire delta. Proves Rank-1 must be 100% locked to 0.54616 peak.

evaluated_pseudo_3500_champion.post_mortem: Direct 95/5 blend without Rank-1 locking allowed 78 Rank-1 predictions to flip, costing -0.00383 on LB. Further confirms the Rank-1 Integrity Law.

candidate_smooth_dual_letterbox_champion.post_mortem: Letterboxing DeiT vision transformer with white margins degraded feature representation: DeiT self-attention across 576 tokens was distracted by artificial white border patches; OOF dropped from 0.42578 to 0.41544, and shifting 29 Rank 1 borderline predictions cost -0.00333 on LB. Proves ConvNeXt-448 is the superior visual backbone.

evaluated_m20_transductive_benchmark.post_mortem: Averaging probability vectors across all students per question implicitly assumed uniform student error, diluting specific error signatures.
